paragraphs.text: Coastal towns face difficult choices as sea levels rise. Engineer Mark Doyle favours building higher sea walls, arguing that they have protected the Dutch coast for centuries and that the cost is small compared with the value of the property behind them.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Geographer Priya Nair disagrees. She points out that sea walls often increase erosion on nearby beaches, and she argues that in some places it would be wiser to allow the sea to flood low-lying farmland, creating salt marshes that absorb the energy of storms.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: The Coastal Communities Group, which represents residents, accepts that some change is unavoidable but insists that no family should be forced to move without fair compensation. It has asked the government to publish long-term plans for each town.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Doyle admits that walls cannot be raised forever. He believes that within fifty years some towns will need to combine walls with natural defences, a view that Nair describes as a welcome step.
paragraphs.label: D

items.quote: no family should be forced to move without fair compensation
items.prompt: wants residents who have to move to be paid fairly

explanation.en: The residents’ group insists that “no family should be forced to move without fair compensation” → C.
explanation.kk: Тұрғындар тобы талап етеді: «no family should be forced to move without fair compensation» → C.
explanation.ru: Группа жителей настаивает: «no family should be forced to move without fair compensation» → C.

items.quote: they have protected the Dutch coast for centuries
items.prompt: refers to the experience of another country

explanation.en: Doyle refers to the Netherlands: walls “have protected the Dutch coast for centuries” → A.
explanation.kk: Дойл Нидерландыға сілтеме жасайды: қабырғалар «have protected the Dutch coast for centuries» → A.
explanation.ru: Дойл ссылается на Нидерланды: стены «have protected the Dutch coast for centuries» → A.

items.quote: it would be wiser to allow the sea to flood low-lying farmland
items.prompt: suggests letting the sea cover some land on purpose

explanation.en: Nair: “it would be wiser to allow the sea to flood low-lying farmland” → B. “On purpose” reflects “allow”.
explanation.kk: Наир: «it would be wiser to allow the sea to flood low-lying farmland» → B. «On purpose» — «allow» дегеннің басқаша айтылымы.
explanation.ru: Наир: «it would be wiser to allow the sea to flood low-lying farmland» → B. «On purpose» пересказывает «allow».

items.quote: It has asked the government to publish long-term plans for each town
items.prompt: has called for long-term plans to be made public

explanation.en: “It has asked the government to publish long-term plans” — the residents’ group → C. “Made public” = “publish”.
explanation.kk: «It has asked the government to publish long-term plans» — бұл тұрғындар тобы → C. «Made public» = «publish».
explanation.ru: «It has asked the government to publish long-term plans» — это группа жителей → C. «Made public» = «publish».

items.quote: Doyle admits that walls cannot be raised forever
items.prompt: accepts that his preferred solution has limits

explanation.en: “Doyle admits that walls cannot be raised forever” → A. Nair, in the same paragraph, only welcomes his view.
explanation.kk: «Doyle admits that walls cannot be raised forever» → A. Сол абзацта Наир оның көзқарасын құптайды ғана, өз тәсілін шектемейді.
explanation.ru: «Doyle admits that walls cannot be raised forever» → A. Наир в том же абзаце лишь одобряет его взгляд, свой подход она не ограничивает.
